teams.heading: Senirusi Seruvakula to remain involved in Flying Fijians coaching setup
teams.body: Senirusi Seruvakula, who was interim coach through July, will remain involved in the Flying Fijians setup, FBC News reports. Mick Byrne left the role in April, and Jake White, the former South Africa coach, was appointed head coach ahead of the 2027 World Cup. White's full backroom staff has yet to be officially confirmed by Fiji. Their last outing was a 34-28 win over Japan.

teams.heading: Jamie George says England squad are 'really upset' by Times rift report
teams.body: The Times report says unhappy players wanted talks with head coach Steve Borthwick and Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney in Argentina in July, citing concerns over man-management. Hooker Jamie George says the squad are unhappy with the article, insisting that "a lot of it's untrue" and that its timing, two days before Sunday's Test against Australia, was designed to divide them. Captain Maro Itoje called a leader's meeting to handle it. "This is going to galvanise us," George said.

lead.why: A fresh on-record reaction from within the squad to the Times player-unrest report, ahead of Sunday's Test.

teams.heading: Oscar Jegou ruled out with rib injury; Esteban Capilla named for Fiji
teams.body: Oscar Jegou is out of Saturday's clash with Fiji after a rib injury sustained in training, and head coach Fabien Galthié has named uncapped loose forward Esteban Capilla in the matchday 23. Capilla could make his France debut off the bench. Kalvin Gourgues gets his first start for Les Bleus in midfield, after four appearances off the bench, in a side already missing Thibaud Flament, Emmanuel Meafou and Matthieu Jalibert.

lead.why: Item 1 is an opinion preview with no news, and items 2 and 3 are older, so this fresh injury-driven squad change is the strongest France story not already reported.

teams.heading: Hugo Keenan hat-trick as Ireland beat Argentina 42-12 at Aviva Stadium
teams.body: Ireland led 21-5 at half-time on Friday night and pulled clear after the break, with Hugo Keenan scoring three tries in the Aviva Stadium win. Dan Sheehan crossed before the interval and Sam Prendergast added a try and five conversions, while Matteo Carreras scored both of Argentina's tries. Keenan's first came in the 15th minute and his third in the 50th, with Ireland finishing 42-12 ahead of Fiji's visit next Saturday.

lead.why: The Friday result is the freshest Ireland event in the pack; the other Ireland items are pre-match previews or ticket warnings.

teams.heading: Quesada hands Leonardo Marin and Paolo Odogwu Italy's centre berths against Springboks
teams.body: Italy coach Gonzalo Quesada has picked Leonardo Marin at inside centre and Paolo Odogwu outside him for Saturday's Test against South Africa in Turin, with Nacho Brex and Tommaso Menoncello both out. Brex has detached a bicep, expects surgery and faces a three-month recovery, while Menoncello is 12 weeks out after subluxing a shoulder for Toulouse against Exeter Chiefs in the Champions Cup. Marin, a former fly-half, was identified by Quesada in June 2025 as a potential successor to Brex's playmaking role.

lead.why: A new injury-driven selection call at centre gives Italy's own squad the day's freshest story, ahead of the Coppa Italia club item and the already-reported Vintcent bench news.

teams.heading: Sione Tuipulotu says Scotland have progressed since 17-17 All Blacks near miss
teams.body: Captain Sione Tuipulotu says the squad has grown since last year's All Blacks match, when Scotland came back from 17-0 down to 17-17 only to lose to a late Damien McKenzie score. "I do feel like we've progressed a lot in the last 12 months," he said. Since then, they have broken England's 12-game winning run, scored 50 points against France and pushed world champions South Africa close in Pretoria. New Zealand have won 31 of the 33 meetings so far.

lead.why: It is a new BBC item with the strongest cross-outlet pickup, and it gives the captain's own view on the squad's progress since last year's near miss, a different angle from the Dempsey story already r

teams.heading: Archie Griffin sits out Wales captain's run but is not injured
teams.body: Bath prop Archie Griffin skipped Friday's captain's run before Saturday's Nations Championship match against Japan at the Principality Stadium. WalesOnline understands he is not carrying an injury and the absence was a decision to manage his training load. He will start at tighthead in a front row featuring Nicky Smith and captain Dewi Lake. The 25-year-old has a reputation as an extremely mobile and dynamic prop.

lead.why: A fresh squad item about a Wales starter's training absence, which beats the Mann feature and the WRU story already reported.

teams.heading: Pumas fall 42-12 to Ireland in Dublin as Hugo Keenan scores hat-trick
teams.body: Argentina went to the Aviva Stadium on Friday night chasing a first win in Dublin and fell well short. BBC Sport had noted beforehand that the Pumas have never won there, and that Ireland had taken 14 of the 20 previous meetings between the sides. Argentina have won all three of their World Cup meetings with Ireland, and each time it ended Ireland's tournament early.

lead.why: It is the only new item about Argentina's own result that is not already covered, since the Camerlinckx signing has run and the other new items are about Ireland or ticketing.

teams.heading: Angus Crichton drops into Wallabies training in England while rehabbing foot injury
teams.body: Wallabies coach Les Kiss says new NSW Waratahs recruit Angus Crichton could be a real asset in the midfield, after the former Sydney Roosters star joined the group for training in England. Crichton, who is still rehabbing a stress fracture in his right foot, was over on holiday and lunched with the squad alongside Brisbane Lions player Will Ashcroft. Kiss said, "I think initially the midfield, definitely. That's how I see it," and Crichton will head to Waratahs pre-season in the coming days.

lead.why: It is the only new item pointing at the Wallabies' own squad, and the McReight cap and Twickenham side have already been covered.

teams.heading: Ieuan Evans recalls 1993 try within 45 seconds against Japan in Cardiff
teams.body: The try came off a wild pass from Japan's scrum-half, a loose ball Evans gathered on the 10-metre line before diving in at the right corner. It was the first full capped match between the sides, and Evans, Wales captain that day, later spoke Japanese at the post-match banquet using phonetic text written by Cardiff University's Business School. Wales won pretty convincingly, and Evans says Japanese rugby has since gone on to become a major force.

lead.why: It is the strongest NEW item in the pack that is not a club contract or a story already covered in earlier editions, though it is a retrospective.

teams.heading: All Blacks could regain No. 1 ranking if Springboks slip in Turin
teams.body: The Springboks' top spot is at stake in Turin on Saturday, where they face Italy in the first Nations Championship match of the weekend. Defeat there would surrender it if paired with an All Blacks victory or draw at Murrayfield. New Zealand cannot drop below second whatever happens, and they have never lost to Scotland.

lead.why: It is a new item with a direct New Zealand stake: the All Blacks return to No. 1 if the Springboks lose in Turin and New Zealand avoid defeat at Murrayfield.

teams.heading: Nacho Brex calls De Allende and Kriel 'probably the best' centre pair
teams.body: Italy's Nacho Brex, who is out injured, told Planet Rugby that Damian de Allende and Jesse Kriel are probably the best centre partnership in the world, adding they have played so many games together that they understand each other's games well. The Springboks' midfield faces an Italy pairing rebuilt around Leonardo Marin and Paolo Odogwu, with Brex's partner Tommaso Menoncello also sidelined for around 12 weeks after a shoulder subluxation. Brex, who detached a bicep in the Top 14, expects surgery next week.

lead.why: It is a fresh, fan-friendly item that puts the Springbok midfield at the centre of the build-up, and it is the only shortlist item that is not a preview, rankings piece or tribute.
